knobs.note: Read by bin/poll-commands.sh as ${TG_TOPICS_SYNC_SECS:-600}. Registered by BH-1165 so it is visible and settable; no reviewed min/max yet, so nothing is clamped.

Read by bin/poll-commands.sh's pause handlers, box-command forwards and box-command expiry block (BH-2657) as ${JOBS_HTTP:-unreachable}: the jobs worker's last HTTP status, set by _jobs_req (bin/lib/jobs/req.sh) and named in a command RESULT. Registered by BH-1685 so it is visible; NOT settable from the control plane — it is a per-call status and a test seam, not an operator knob; nothing is clamped.

Read by bin/poll-commands.sh's box-command expiry block as ${BOX_CONSOLE_COMMANDS_TTL_S:-300}: a forwarded console command still queued after this many seconds is expired, failure-beaten and alerted. Keep it equal to the box-console-commands lane's knob of the same name.

Read by bin/poll-commands.sh's pause_board handler as ${JOBS_BODY:-}: the jobs worker's last response body, set by _jobs_req (bin/lib/jobs/req.sh), from which the RESULT's expires_at is read. Registered so it is visible; NOT settable from the control plane — it is a per-call response and a test seam, not an operator knob; nothing is clamped.

Read by bin/poll-commands.sh's pause_board handler: the ttl_s a console board pause sends when its payload carries none, so the triage pause row always has an explicit expiry instead of the worker's generic pause_default_ttl_s (86400), which ended board pauses silently after 24h. A payload ttl_s wins; a value that is not a positive integer falls back to 604800 (the worker's one-week ceiling). The command RESULT names the stored expires_at, and bin/pipeline-health.sh warns PAUSE_EXPIRY_WARN_S before it.
